title: P1: consent bypass — prompt=none/prompt=login grants all requested scopes without explicit user consent
description:
When a cached PB account exists and prompt=none is requested, the UI silently POSTs the PB token back to /auth. When prompt=login, the UI authenticates and immediately posts the token — never showing a consent screen. Server-side oauth2_auth.go grants every requested scope unconditionally once any valid pb_token arrives.

Evidence:
- ui/src/login.ts:142-155 (silent prompt=none flow)
- ui/src/login.ts:392-407 (auto-consent after login)
- oauth2_auth.go:122-126 (unconditional GrantScope loop)

Fix: introduce a _oauth2Consents collection keyed by (user_id, client_id) recording the scopes the user has granted previously. /auth must:
  1. For prompt=none: only proceed if a matching consent row covers ALL requested scopes; otherwise return interaction_required.
  2. For prompt=login: reauthenticate AND require an explicit consent screen unless covered by existing consent.
  3. Without prompt: default to showing consent for any scope not yet granted.

Pair with lr7 (login-handoff): once interactions are server-managed, the consent decision can be recorded on the interaction object before completion.
close_reason: /login/complete requires explicit decision=approve|deny. Approve checks (consented_scopes ∪ prior _oauth2Consents row) covers requested_scopes; insufficient coverage returns consent_required redirect. Approved scopes are upserted into _oauth2Consents so future prompt=none flows can proceed silently if the existing consent already covers the request. UI POSTs consented_scopes on the consent button; declineConsent sends decision=deny.

title: P1: login-handoff state is unsigned — PB auth token exfiltration to attacker redirect_uri
description:
Login UI base64-URL-decodes the state JSON and unconditionally POSTs {pb_token, pb_token_iat} to whatever redirect_uri is encoded inside it. No HMAC, signature, server-side lookup, nonce, or origin restriction. An attacker can craft state with their own redirect_uri, lure a victim to /oauth2/login?state=<crafted>, and receive the victim's first-party PocketBase auth token after they authenticate.

Evidence:
- ui/src/login.ts:426-460 (state parsing)
- ui/src/login.ts:405-407 (token POST)
- ui/src/lib/utils.ts:35-55 (generic form POST)
- oauth2_auth.go:88-103 (server constructs JSON state, no HMAC)

Fix: replace browser-controlled state with a server-owned interaction ID. /auth stores the AuthorizeRequester payload in a new _oauth2Interactions collection keyed by random UUID; the redirect to /login carries only that opaque ID. The UI POSTs the pb_token back to a same-origin completion endpoint that looks up the interaction, validates expiry + binding, and completes the Fosite request. Until then, an HMAC over the state JSON using GlobalSecret is a stopgap.
close_reason: Browser-controlled state JSON blob removed. /auth stores a server-side Interaction (_oauth2Interactions collection) and redirects to /login?interaction_id=X. UI fetches metadata from /login/state and submits credentials to /login/complete which reconstructs the OAuth request from server-stored params. redirect_uri the server uses ALWAYS sourced from the Interaction. Legacy pb_token-in-form path removed from /auth. TestLoginInteractionFlow covers 5 scenarios.

title: P2: OAUTH2_MASTER_KEY raw-32 short-circuit accepts low-entropy 32-char passphrases
description:
decodeMasterKey treats len(raw)==32 as a raw 32-byte master key. Users will inevitably set a 32-character memorable password (e.g. 'MySuperSecretKeyForOAuth2Plugin!!') instead of 32 cryptographically random bytes. Entropy drops from ~256 bits to ~150-210 bits, weakening at-rest encryption.

Fix:
- Add a Shannon-entropy estimate on len==32 input; if < 4.5 bits/byte (rough heuristic for printable ASCII passphrases), reject with a clear error pointing operators at hex/base64 encoding.
- Alternatively: remove the raw-32 short-circuit entirely and document that base64 or hex is required. This is the cleanest fix.
- README: add a warning + show how to generate via openssl rand -base64 32.
close_reason: decodeMasterKey len==32 path runs requireHighEntropy: rejects all-printable-ASCII (~99.99% of random 32B has >=1 non-printable) and <2.5 bits/byte (catches repeated patterns). Tests cover all paths.

title: P2: xpb plugin enables RFC 7591 dynamic client registration by default — anyone can mint OAuth clients
description:
xpb/plugin.go defaults EnableRFC7591DynamicClientRegistration=true. The /oauth2/register route is public when enabled and requires only non-empty redirect_uris. Any unauthenticated network caller in a packaged deployment can mint OAuth clients, then initiate full authorization-code flows. Combined with lr7+mci this is full end-to-end attacker chain.

Evidence:
- xpb/plugin.go:17-23 (default-on)
- oauth2.go (route mount, public)
- oauth2_register.go:57-67 (no auth, minimal validation)

Fix:
- Flip the xpb plugin default to false.
- When the flag is on, require either an admin token (PB superuser auth) OR an Initial Access Token (RFC 7591 §3) configurable per-tenant.
- Add redirect_uri policy (HTTPS-only, no localhost in prod, no wildcards by default) + rate limit.
- Tests: spammable registration with no auth should fail in test app.
close_reason: RFC 7591 DCR: xpb plugin default flipped to false. Config gains DynamicClientRegistrationInitialAccessTokens + AllowUnauthenticatedDynamicClientRegistration; Register() fails closed if DCR is on without either gate. /register handler enforces constant-time Bearer-token match. Redirect-URI policy enforces HTTPS-or-loopback + no fragments + absolute URIs. Tests: 3 IAT scenarios (missing/wrong/valid) + 6 redirect-URI cases.

title: P2: OAuth2 access token revocation only partially effective — PB-native JWT still valid post-revoke
description:
Access tokens are PB native auth tokens (user.NewStaticAuthToken). /oauth2/revoke deletes the _oauth2Access row but PocketBaseStrategy.ValidateAccessToken calls FindAuthRecordByToken which validates the JWT directly without consulting the OAuth2 session table. After revoke:
- RequireScope-gated routes correctly reject (they go through fosite.IntrospectToken which hits _oauth2Access).
- PB-native endpoints using apis.RequireAuth() still accept the token until its natural JWT exp.
- UserInfo: routes that don't go through RequireScope are vulnerable.

Fix options:
A) Change PocketBaseStrategy.ValidateAccessToken to look up _oauth2Access in addition to FindAuthRecordByToken, AND fail if row absent/revoked.
B) On revoke, also blacklist the token signature in a small allow/deny store consulted by PB validation (requires PB hook into auth path — may not be feasible without PB upstream cooperation).
C) Document the limitation prominently and recommend short-lived access tokens.

Recommendation: implement (A) — adds one DB read per token validation; cost acceptable given the security gain. Document the cache contract explicitly.
close_reason: Revocation now strongly enforceable: (1) ValidateAccessToken also requires the _oauth2Access row to exist (defense in depth — fosite introspection + RequireScope already use this path). (2) New public RevokedTokenGuard(app) middleware for PB-native routes that need OAuth-side revocation to take effect. Tests cover live-token-allows, revoked-token-rejects, missing-bearer-rejects.

title: P2: key rotation kid written but decrypt always uses active master
description: kid written in crypto.go:192 but decrypt always uses the active master and fingerprint mismatch hard-fails (params.go:141). Acceptable only if v1 documents the master is immutable and the recovery path is restore-from-backup or rewrap. Otherwise: add multi-key decrypt (look up DEK by kid in a keyring), re-encrypt on read, and document the rotation procedure.
close_reason: MasterKeyringProvider interface + env-backed Keyring() reading OAUTH2_MASTER_KEY_OLD (comma-separated history). openEnvelopeWithKeyring picks a master by env.Kid; row is lazily rewrapped against the active master via CAS update. verifyOrWriteFingerprint accepts any keyring member during rotation and promotes the sentinel to active. README documents the rotation procedure. Verified by TestLoadParam_KeyRotation_RewrapsOnRead + TestOpenEnvelopeWithKeyring_KidLookup.

title: P2: consent decline access_denied not handled server-side
description: UI posts error=access_denied (login.ts:359) on user decline. Server switch in oauth2_auth.go:45 does not handle access_denied and falls through to ErrServerError. Fix: add case access_denied → fosite.ErrAccessDenied in the switch, include iss per RFC 9207.
close_reason: access_denied case added to consent-error switch — returns fosite.ErrAccessDenied (not server_error). Verified by TestAuthEndpoint_AccessDeniedRedirect.

title: P2: saveParamValue re-fetch+overwrite can lose concurrent updates
description: params.go:153 reads then blindly overwrites. Two concurrent real-param updates: T1 reads v1, T2 reads v1, T1 writes v2, T2 writes v3 over v2 (or vice versa). Legacy-migration path at params.go:243 logs save failures and returns decoded data so two legacy readers racing mostly converge, but normal updates race. Fix: optimistic UPDATE WHERE updated=:expected or conditional writes per key, mirror the markRefreshRotated pattern shipped on fix/codex-p1-middleware-and-refresh-race.
close_reason: saveParamValue split into create-only path + updateParamValueCAS value-based compare-and-swap. Concurrent envelope migrations no longer last-writer-wins; create-race recovery reads the winner's row and decodes it. Verified by TestUpdateParamValueCAS_BlocksStaleWrite.

title: P2: RFC 9207 iss missing on authorize error responses
description: oauth2_auth.go:172 adds iss only after successful NewAuthorizeResponse. Error paths at oauth2_auth.go:36, 48, 164 call WriteAuthorizeError without iss. RFC 9207 requires iss on both success AND error redirectable authorization responses. Fix: wrap WriteAuthorizeError sites so iss is appended to the redirect URL before write.
close_reason: All 4 WriteAuthorizeError call sites route through writeAuthorizeErrorWithIss, which mirrors fosite's error-redirect logic with iss= appended for query/fragment/form_post. JSON path (invalid redirect_uri) deliberately omits iss per RFC 9207 §2.3. Tests verify iss on both access_denied and login_required redirects.

title: P2: HKDF info bound to DataDir breaks decryption on path change
description: crypto.go:160 binds DEK derivation to app.DataDir(). Moving the tenant data dir, cwd-relative path changes, or symlink swaps make existing envelopes undecryptable. Fix: use a stable stored per-app encryption context/salt (e.g. random uuid persisted on first write), with a fallback-decrypt-then-rewrap migration path for envelopes derived from the old DataDir context.
close_reason: Per-app envelope ctxID (UUID at oauth2_envelope_ctx_id) replaces app.DataDir() as HKDF info source. Legacy envelopes seal-bound to DataDir still decrypt via openEnvelopeWithKeyring fallback and are rewrapped under the ctxID on read. Verified by TestLoadParam_DataDirChange + TestOpenEnvelopeWithKeyring_LegacyDataDirFallback.

title: P3: integration test for full authorization-code flow + revocation-actually-blocks test
description:
Existing tests cover endpoint smoke checks and isolation but not the full code-+-PKCE flow end-to-end (auth -> login interaction -> callback -> /token -> /userinfo). Also missing: a test that revokes an access token and asserts subsequent requests fail (which will currently FAIL — exposes wg6).

Add two scenarios in examples/multitenant or tests/:
1. happy path: full code+PKCE flow with state echo + iss check
2. revocation: mint token, /revoke, attempt /userinfo -> 401 (will fail until wg6 fixed; gate accordingly or mark as known-broken)
close_reason: TestFullAuthCodeFlow_EndToEnd_PKCE drives /auth → /login/complete → /token → /userinfo (RequireScope-gated) and asserts /api/widgets goes 200→401 after /revoke (proves wg6 closure end-to-end). TestLoginInteractionFlow covers 5 sub-scenarios on the lr7+mci redesign.

title: P3: bump RSA signing key from 2048 to 3072 bits for new keys; document rotation
description:
loadPrivateKeyFromAppStorage generates RSA 2048. NIST recommends 3072+ for keys with multi-year lifetimes. 2048 acceptable until ~2030 but new deployments should mint stronger.

Fix:
- Change rsa.GenerateKey size to 3072 for new key generation.
- Existing 2048-bit keys keep working (do not force re-mint — that would invalidate all live tokens).
- Document a key-rotation procedure: delete the _params row for oauth2_rsa_key, restart, new 3072-bit key generated. ID tokens signed with the old key will fail until clients refresh JWKS.
close_reason: rsaSigningKeyBits=3072. Existing 2048 keys keep working.

title: P3: remove redundant sanitizeHeaderValue and dead r.POST on metadata endpoints
description:
Two small cleanups:

1) middleware.go sanitizeHeaderValue is unnecessary when used with fmt.Sprintf %q (Go already quote-escapes). Delete the helper and use %q directly.

2) oauth2.go handleJSON registers OPTIONS, GET, AND POST routes but the handler rejects non-GET with 405. POST registration is dead code. Remove r.POST(path, h).
close_reason: sanitizeHeaderValue removed (Go %q handles it). handleJSON no longer registers dead r.POST.

title: P3: replace mohae/deepcopy (unmaintained since 2017)
description: github.com/mohae/deepcopy is unmaintained — last commit Sept 2017. Audit its use in this repo; if cloneConfig + cloneStrings + cloneBytes already cover the only need, drop the dep entirely. Otherwise implement manual clone methods or switch to a maintained alternative.
close_reason: session.go no longer imports mohae/deepcopy; hand-clone via maps.Clone + slice copies. Indirect via fosite remains.

title: P3: replace pkg/errors with stdlib fmt.Errorf %w
description:
github.com/pkg/errors is deprecated (last commit 2020). Modern Go uses fmt.Errorf with %w verb for error wrapping. Used pervasively in params.go, crypto.go, instance.go, oauth2.go. Mechanical refactor; tests unaffected.

Fix: codemod errors.Wrap(err, msg) -> fmt.Errorf("msg: %w", err) and errors.New -> stdlib errors.New (already aliased). Drop the import.
close_reason: pkg/errors purged from all 6 files. Wrap -> fmt.Errorf %w; Errorf -> fmt.Errorf; New stays on stdlib errors.

title: P3: registrationGuard sync.Map leaks entries on dynamic tenant teardown
description:
registrationGuard never has entries removed except via ResetStateForTests. Long-running processes that create/destroy tenant apps dynamically accumulate stale interface-value entries. Memory leak is small but real.

Fix: expose public Deregister(app core.App) that calls registrationGuard.Delete(app) and clears app.Store() of storeKey/registeringKey. Document the API for multi-tenant operators.
close_reason: Public Deregister(app) added; ResetStateForTests delegates. Clears app.Store keys + registrationGuard.

title: P3: hardcoded 6h session ExpiresAt independent of AccessTokenLifespan config
description:
session.go:30 sets Claims.ExpiresAt = time.Now().Add(time.Hour * 6) unconditionally. AccessTokenLifespan is configurable via fosite.Config but the session's ExpiresAt ignores it. ID-token expiry will mismatch access-token lifespan whenever the operator configures a non-6h lifespan.

Fix: wire ExpiresAt from cfg.GetAccessTokenLifespan() (or a dedicated IDTokenLifespan in Config).
close_reason: Session.Claims.ExpiresAt left zero; fosite computes from Config.GetIDTokenLifespan.

title: P3: PAR + DPoP out of v1 scope unless targeting FAPI
description: PAR (RFC 9126 pushed authorization request) not required for v1 unless FAPI/high-assurance is in scope. Would need fosite PAR factory, endpoint, PARStorage, discovery metadata. Same for DPoP sender-constrained tokens. Document this decision in README or ARCHITECTURE so it stops coming up in reviews; revisit if FAPI conformance becomes a goal.
close_reason: README Scope & Roadmap section documents PAR/DPoP/mTLS as deliberately out of v1 scope. FAPI conformance noted as separate epic trigger.

title: P3: decodeMasterKey only supports base64/hex, not raw 32-byte env
description: crypto.go:96 decodeMasterKey decodes base64 or hex. If docs/env-var help claim raw 32-byte strings work, fix one or the other. Either accept raw 32-byte values (len==32 short-circuit) or correct the docs to specify base64/hex only.
close_reason: decodeMasterKey: len==32 short-circuit accepts raw master key. Tests cover raw/hex/base64 formats. Docs updated.

title: P3: demo seedClient contract-coupled to create hook; ignores hash errors
description: examples/multitenant/integration_test.go:158 + oauth2.go:282 — seedClient relies on the create hook's exact contract. Add an assertion or comment. The create hook itself ignores bcrypt hash errors silently — at minimum log them or return an error so a misconfigured cost factor fails loudly in dev.
close_reason: OnRecordCreate hook now returns error on hash failure (no silent plaintext). Demo seedClient documents the contract assumption explicitly.

title: P3: RequireScope doc says bearer header but accepts form/query token
description: middleware.go uses fosite.AccessTokenFromRequest which per fosite/introspect.go:22 also accepts access_token in form/query in addition to Authorization: Bearer. If header-only resource auth is the intent, parse Authorization directly and reject query/form. Otherwise update the godoc to match reality.
close_reason: RequireScope now header-only via bearerTokenFromHeader(). Query+form token paths return 401. Godoc updated to document the intent. Regression tests added.
